name: Submission Package Builder
description: Once a client's readiness score clears the bar, this workflow automatically gathers the homepage/policy screenshots, live policy text, and already-uploaded documents a verification submission needs, and emails you all the pieces. Simplification: since this platform has no PDF-merge node, the pieces are delivered as individual links rather than one combined PDF.

notes.what: Works like an alarm clock — runs your workflow automatically at a specific time you set each day
notes.overview: Runs your workflow automatically on a schedule using a simple time picker. Select your time (HH:MM format) and timezone, and the workflow will execute daily at that time. Great for daily reports, periodic checks, or recurring tasks.
tips: Use 24-hour format (e.g., 09:00 for 9 AM, 14:30 for 2:30 PM)
Select your timezone from the dropdown (IST, UTC, etc.)
Workflow runs daily at the specified time
Test with manual trigger first
Timezone conversion is handled automatically
notes.why: Polls for clients who have cleared the readiness bar. One client per run.

notes.what: Reads rows from an Airtable base or adds new records — like a smarter spreadsheet
notes.overview: List, get, create, update, upsert, and delete Airtable records. The resource dropdown is visual only; runtime implements record operations, not table-management APIs.
tips: Use a Personal Access Token with data.records scopes or a saved Airtable connection
Base ID plus table/tableId are required for every operation
Create/update/upsert return records/count
Upsert also returns created and updated counts
Delete returns deletedRecords/count, not top-level deleted:true
notes.why: Picks up one ready client whose package has not been built yet.

notes.what: Writes and runs any JavaScript you like to transform or process your data
notes.overview: Run sandboxed JavaScript once against the current workflow data and return the transformed value for downstream nodes.
tips: Always return the value the next node should receive
Default timeout is 5000ms and runtime caps at 30000ms
Use Output Schema such as {"type":"object"} only as a top-level shape hint
JavaScript has no credentials; connect downstream service node accounts separately
Do not paste API keys, tokens, or passwords into code
notes.why: Lifts the client's website, name and email to the top level for the steps below.

notes.what: Calls any web URL and gets data back — your universal connector to the internet
notes.overview: Call an external API or webhook, optionally adding headers, query parameters, body data, and a timeout.
notes.why: Captures the homepage and policy pages as images, which verification submissions usually require as evidence. Needs your own screenshot API key — replace the placeholder.

notes.what: Calls any web URL and gets data back — your universal connector to the internet
notes.overview: Call an external API or webhook, optionally adding headers, query parameters, body data, and a timeout.
notes.why: Pulls the live privacy policy and terms text so the submission quotes what is actually published today.

notes.what: Upload, download, list, or delete files in your Google Drive
notes.overview: List, upload, or download files in Google Drive. The Delete option is shown in the dropdown but is not implemented by the runtime executor â€” selecting it always fails.
tips: Leave Folder ID empty to list/upload across the whole Drive, not just the root
File IDs are in the URL: /file/d/FILE_ID/view
Upload requires base64, plain text, or a data URL for File Data
Download returns dataBase64 for binary files (PDFs, images), or content for text/JSON files
Delete is not implemented â€” it always fails with "Unsupported Google Drive operation: delete"
notes.why: Collects the documents already on file so the package is complete rather than partial.

config.subject: Submission package ready for {{input.businessName}}

notes.what: Send emails from your Gmail account or read and search messages in your inbox
notes.overview: Send, list, get, or search Gmail messages. Send recipients can be typed manually or extracted from upstream/fallback Google Sheets rows.
tips: Connect Google OAuth in Connections; do not paste tokens into workflow fields
Gmail search syntax: from:, subject:, is:unread, has:attachment
List/Search only return {id, threadId} per message â€” use a Get step with that id for full content
Body is plain text only
Get returns Gmail's raw API message; the body text is base64url-encoded inside message.payload.body.data
Use search to filter messages before getting details
notes.why: Delivers every piece needed for the submission in one email. Pieces are sent as separate links because the platform has no PDF-merge step.

notes.what: Combines results coming from two paths into one
notes.overview: Rejoins multiple workflow branches and combines their data into one payload for the next step.
tips: Use overwrite for simple flat objects when duplicate keys can be replaced.
Use append when the next node should receive a list at {{$json.items}}.
Use deep_merge when branches add different nested details that should survive together.
Connect every branch that should rejoin into Merge, then connect Merge output to the final action.
notes.why: Joins the screenshot and policy-text branches. Without this join the email could only ever see one of the two.

notes.what: Reads rows from an Airtable base or adds new records — like a smarter spreadsheet
notes.overview: List, get, create, update, upsert, and delete Airtable records. The resource dropdown is visual only; runtime implements record operations, not table-management APIs.
tips: Use a Personal Access Token with data.records scopes or a saved Airtable connection
Base ID plus table/tableId are required for every operation
Create/update/upsert return records/count
Upsert also returns created and updated counts
Delete returns deletedRecords/count, not top-level deleted:true
notes.why: Stamps the client as packaged so the same package is not rebuilt and re-emailed every 15 minutes.

notes.what: Makes a yes/no decision: if something is true, go one way; otherwise go another
notes.overview: Makes a yes/no decision from previous-step data and routes matching work through TRUE and non-matching work through FALSE.
tips: Use the builder for normal setup; use JSON mode only when pasting prepared condition objects.
Choose AND when every row must match; choose OR when any row can match.
Use equals for statuses and categories, greater-than operators for numeric thresholds, and contains for text or lists.
Connect both TRUE and FALSE outputs so no business case silently disappears.
notes.why: Most polls find nothing. Without this the workflow screenshotted a blank URL and emailed an empty package every 15 minutes.
